items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to join him again

ctx.x: How did you meet? How did you audition for him or get that spot?

Well, let’s see I’m trying to think had I been with Andy Kirk? No, I don’t think so. But he needed a tenor, and he wasn’t too well known, you know? And he was glad for me to be with his band. Then I worked with that band. But later then he went back to Benny Moten, Hot Lips Page, all of those guys, they went back with Benny, with Benny Moten. So then when Benny Moten died — oh yeah, Walter Page, I don’t want to leave him out, when Benny died, Basie was the one that took over the band, then he sent and got me to…
And what year was this when you first started with the Basie band?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: And of course, I stayed with that band until I joined Basie in '39

ctx.x: I think he took that. Really, I don't know. But we called him -- did we call him Sir Charles then? I think we did. It must have come out of Nat Toles' band. And of course, I stayed with that band until I joined Basie in '39 and that's -- that was from Omaha, Nebraska. We had a better band at the time. You know, I've been -- this was miswritten one time. I said one time that when Basie took -- when Basie was -- John Hammond took Basie, bandwise, we were -- we had a better band.

items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: Okay, so Buddy came next and Buddy came into Hershel's spot.

ctx.x: They both went in the Army.
Okay, so Buddy came next and Buddy came into Hershel's spot. Is that right, the big sound?
